text:
maria: Heads up — we've got prefetch pool saturation in prod this morning, causing cascading demotes and noisy evictions for small tenants. Thinking we add per-tenant soft quotas + a preemption path for runaway tenants. Any immediate objections?

alex: Can you drop the panels / sample traces? how bad is "noisy" here?

sam: Eviction-rate for small-tenants up ~3x during the burst. p99 latency stable but read-after-write anomalies spiked (see https://grafana.fake/r/abc123).

lee: Soft quota sounds reasonable. My mental model: keep a shared pool but give each tenant a token-bucket; if a tenant exhausts tokens, mark their prefetches as low-priority and allow preemption. Avoid hard isolation.

nadia: We need to be careful about correctness: demote + async handoff currently can surface older KV versions if a read races with a demote that doesn't complete the lease handshake. We must ensure demote either drains outstanding reads or preserves read-after-write for pinned prefixes.

jorge: Sketch of API change: demote_sync(prefix) -> blocks until lease revoked + IO quiesced; demote_async(prefix) -> start background migration and mark as demoting. Consumers can opt in. Pseudocode:```
// eviction decision (simplified)
if tenant_tokens(tenant) < threshold and global_pool_saturated:
    mark_prefetches_low_priority(tenant)
    if tenant_is_top_hotspot:
        preempt(tenant) // force demote_sync on hot prefixes
else:
    normal_evict()
```

alex: Tradeoffs — demote_sync will add tail latency (blocking), but gives safer RA/W semantics. Hybrid: soft-preempt immediately throttles prefetches; escalate to demote_sync only if preempted tenant keeps thrashing.

maria: Proposal for experiments: run A/B for 2 weeks across a subset of machines: 1) baseline shared-only, 2) shared + per-tenant soft quota (token-bucket), 3) soft quota + escalation to demote_sync for top-1% hot tenants. Capture: eviction-rate, demote-sync invocations, p99 generation latency, stale-read-counter, and cost-per-1000-requests.

lee: Add metrics: demote_conflict_count, prefetch_throttle_retries, tenant_token_burst_consumed. Also emit a trace span when escalation happens.

nadia: Add unit/integration test: fake-clock + concurrent reader/writer + demote async path to assert no stale-visible state for writes that commit before demote call. If hard, add opt-in kernel that pins recently-written prefixes.

sam: I'll own the infra + dashboards for the experiment. jorge can prototype token-bucket and escalation logic in a feature branch. lee will wire metrics. nadia will write the tests.

maria: timeline — prototype in 1 week, internal canary in next week, run A/B for 2 weeks. If metrics look good, we can schedule a rollout.

alex: one more thought — consider a reactive backpressure signal to clients (429-like) when tenant prefetches are being preempted so upstream can slow down.

jorge: noted, will add an optional response-header and SDK helper to expose a "prefetch-throttled" flag.

maria: sweet. thanks all :thumbsup:
